title: Amoebic liver abscess (pus pocket in the liver)

items: An amoeba (a single-celled parasite called Entamoeba histolytica) can spread from the gut to the liver and form a pocket of pus (abscess).
It is most often seen in people who have lived in or travelled to areas where amoebiasis is common.
Fever and pain in the upper right side of the belly, where the liver is.
Jaundice (yellow skin and eyes) is rare.
Diarrhoea is absent in most people, so no diarrhoea does not rule the infection out.
Ultrasound or CT scan of the abdomen.
A stool test for the amoeba.
A blood test for amoeba antibodies (serology). It can be normal early, so it may need repeating.
A needle drainage (aspiration) if there is no improvement in 5 to 7 days, the abscess is large or on the left side, or the diagnosis is unclear.
Your doctor will choose the treatment for the infection.
Take any prescribed medicine as directed, and ask your doctor before changing it.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Tell your doctor about any past travel or past residence in areas where amoebiasis is common.
Rest and drink fluids while you recover.
Your doctor may repeat blood tests or scans to check that the abscess is shrinking.
Tell your doctor if you are not better after 5 to 7 days.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: The source entry lists no specific emergency sign for this condition.
Get urgent help if you feel suddenly much worse, or have new severe pain or confusion.
